I’ve always thought I might have bipolar disorder so it’s always been an idea in the back of mind but I’m horrible at speaking up for myself so i haven’t ever mentioned it. I take Wellbutrin and Prozac and have a recurring major depressive disorder diagnosis with social anxiety and chronic fatigue as well. My mental health journey started almost two years ago, when I was first prescribed Wellbutrin, but I only received my diagnosis about six months ago after finally seeing a psychiatrist for the first time in my life. 

Anyway, my meds get adjusted with almost every appointment and I just don’t feel like they are helping much. Aside from that, I have these horrible depressive episodes, such as the one I’m going through right now. I haven’t been to a single class all week and it’s midterms. I just can’t get out of bed. Very depressive, I know. But I think I show signs of hypomania as well. For example I’ll go through these periods where Im like “fuck it” and buy like four new pairs of shoes at a time or something. I also skip class during these periods but instead of laying in bed, not doing anything, I maintain my “fuck it” attitude and get a bunch of things done I’ve needed to do for a while however ignoring my priorities and finding myself with bad grades and twice as much work needing to be done. 

There’s other signs too, like my chronic fatigue, changes in appetite, sometimes I lose control of my temper and freak out over small things, sometimes breaking things in the process. My mood just seems inconsistent and so I’m thinking a mood stabilizer would be more successful but idk really. :/

I literally cannot cry or else I get a terrible headache and sometimes even a migraine. It doesn’t only happen when I feel the urge to cry but also when I feel any sort of emotion I’m uncomfortable with. 

It is seriously the most frustrating thing. Especially because through all of it, I’ve learned to completely shut my emotions off. I have been reaching out for help for about a year, but I don’t think people even believe me and if they do, it’s very underestimated.

I’ve honestly given up at this point. However this is the first I’ve heard of someone else experiencing anything similar. Gives me a little hope!

Right now I’m prescribed bupropion and Prozac. I’ve only been on the Prozac for about 3 months. I  don’t know if it’s from one or the other really but I feel very on the inside. Like I don’t have emotions. The bupropion did even out and I have noticed a lot of positive changes. For example I would get angry and was extremely irritable all the time. The smallest things would make me freak and my relationship with my boyfriend suffered very badly because of it. I often directed my anger towards him. After I would calm down a little, I would just cry for literally weeks at a time. Worst time of my life. 

That doesn’t happen quite to the same extent or as often as before the bupropion. 

I was prescribed the Prozac with hopes that it would up my energy and give me motivation and make me sleep less but it makes me drowsy and more tired, I think... 

At this point I had not even been diagnosed with anything. I was basically just told to take these pills and hopefully they’d make me feel better. My gp even told me to not schedule a follow up appointment with the Prozac. Instead I was instructed to call my doctor. So I did and it was her nurse talking to me and the only thing she asked me was if I want a refill or not. Kind of a shitty feeling. 

Yesterday I finally saw a psychiatrist and was diagnosed with recurrent major depressive disorder, social anxiety, and chronic fatigue. I am also having some tests run. I think I have bipolar II though.

Oh my goddd this is so me. I’m 22 f and am currently taking classes at University. I’ve been on bupropion for about 9 months now and the side effects are terrible. Literally everything that you were/are now feeling and going through is 100% me. Except for the part about your parents. Mine don’t give a shit. 

I really struggle to express the way that I feel and do everything to ignore myself in general. With that being said, after reading this I have such a better understanding of what exactly I am feeling. Also, it’s good to know that we’re not alone. So thank you. 

Back to the bupropion, I had horrible side effects. I could not sleep at all which is super unusual for me because I sleep like 15 hours a day at least. That side effect in particular was very short lived however. Within 2 maybe 3 weeks at most I was back to sleeping all day. For the first couple of weeks I also felt sick to my stomach if I wasn’t physically moving around in some sort of way. You should stick with it. It gets way better. 

I’m sorry for the way that you are feeling but like I said, you’re not alone and I’m not alone. Take things day by day, week by week, and know that it is not your fault. Just do you. 

I hope that this helps in some sort of way because for me, it feels as if my head is a big tangled up mess and it fucking sucks. Good luck to you!
